newsitem.title: USA: China MFN loss would raise U.S. prices -retailers.
newsitem.headline: China MFN loss would raise U.S. prices -retailers.

text.p: Ending normal trade relations with China would cost American consumers hundreds of dollars a year in higher prices for shoes, toys, clothes and many other products, U.S. retailers said on Monday.

The National Retail Federation released a survey showing the potential impact on consumers' pocketbooks if Congress voted to overturn President Bill Clinton's decision to renew China's Most Favored Nation (MFN) trade status.

Prices of toys manufactured in China would rise dramatically, putting such popular items as Mattel Inc. unit Tyco Toys' "Tickle Me Elmo" stuffed animal out of the reach of many families, the group said.

China is the cheapest supplier of toys and although many items are also available from other countries, prices would be higher, the group said. The retail price of a "Tickle Me Elmo" toy would rise from $29.99 to $49.70, the group said.
There is no duty on many toys imported from China and loss of MFN would result in a 90 percent tarifff.

The duty on a silk blouse would rise from 7.4 percent to 65 percent, the retail group said. A $10 pair of sneakers would double in price while the tariff on disk drives would rise to $35 percent from zero.
The group estimated that the tariff increases could cost an average U.S. household about $302 a year.
Only a handful of countries are denied MFN trade status. The House of Representatives is expected to vote this month on a resolution that would deny the trade privilege to Beijing.

Analysts expect a close vote because of lawmakers' concerns about human rights abuses, nuclear technology transfers, the huge U.S. trade deficit with China and allegations that Beijing tried to influence U.S. elections through illegal campaign contributions.
